---
title: "Chart viewer"
subtitle: "An interactive mathematical illustration"
---

Inspect the sine curve using the chart's own controls: hover for values, drag a
rectangle to zoom, choose Pan to move, and use Reset axes to return. Expand
opens the interactive HTML in a floating window. Askr provides the frame and
window controls; Plotly draws and operates this example.

## Inline chart

The curve is a public mathematical illustration of $y = \sin(x)$, not a solver
result. Its data, Plotly JavaScript and author-selected colors are contained in
one local HTML file. It makes no runtime CDN request.

{{< askr-chart-view src="images/plotly-example.html" label="Inspect the sine curve" >}}

The chart's light background and blue line are deliberate author choices.
Changing the Askr theme changes the surrounding controls, while the chart keeps
those colors. The floating chart is a separate view: it begins with its own
axes, and its zoom does not replace the inline chart's state.

## Button-only entry

A page can offer a larger view without placing another chart in the article:

{{< askr-chart-view src="images/plotly-example.html" mode="button" label="Open interactive chart" >}}

Close the window or press Escape to return to reading. The chart's own toolbar
supplies its zoom, pan and reset commands; this window has no second set of
Askr image controls.

See the [Chart viewer guide](../usage/chart-viewer.qmd) for authoring and trusted
HTML requirements, or [Image viewer](image-viewer.qmd) for static pictures.
The example's [HTML source](images/plotly-example.html) and
[Plotly MIT license](images/plotly-example.LICENSE.txt) are included locally.
